children: ChatGPT maker’s September revenue run rate was below the figure previously circulated. Accounting differences explain much of the gap, but AI stocks still sold off.
OpenAI’s annualized revenue approached $50 billion at September’s end, below the roughly $70 billion previously indicated to investors, the Financial Times reported.
Different treatment of cloud-partner sales explains much of the gap. Anthropic includes sales through partners such as AWS and Google Cloud in its revenue figures, while OpenAI’s calculation differs.
Attempts to make the companies directly comparable contributed to the earlier $70 billion estimate, according to sources.

Annualized revenue is a pace, not a completed year’s sales cycle. Multiplying a month’s revenue by 12 produces a run rate: approximately $4.2 billion monthly would imply $50 billion annually. That helps describe growth, but it does not establish full-year revenue, profit or cash generated.
📉 A private company moves public markets
AI-linked stocks absorbed the disappointment Thursday. Nvidia fell 2.9%, Micron lost 4.8%, Broadcom dropped 4.3% and Intel slid 5.3%. The

The $70 billion figure remains a reported year-end ambition. Bloomberg subsequently reported that OpenAI expects to reach or exceed that annualized level by December, largely through enterprise growth.
Moving from September’s $50 billion would require approximately 40% growth in the run rate — a forecast investors can now track.
📊 Growth must support the funding ambitions

OpenAI is discussing another fundraising round of at least $30 billion, Bloomberg reported, targeting a $1.4 trillion valuation before the new money. Against the current revenue pace, that implies roughly 28 times annualized sales.
Rapid sales growth still leaves substantial financing needs. The FT reported projected cash burn approaching $280 billion through 2030 as OpenAI expands infrastructure.
The next test is consistent financial disclosure: revenue measured on the same basis over time, margins and cash requirements. OpenAI has
